sentences.text:
Appellant :- Akhilesh Singh
Respondent :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Appellant :- Usha Srivastava, Ashutosh Tripathi, Jitendra Singh, Saurabh Tri
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A., Kuldeep Singh
Hon'ble Ashwani Kumar Mishra,J.
Hon'ble Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.
(Per: Hon'ble Ashwani Kumar Mishra, J.)
1.

This criminal appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 27.9.2018 passed by Additional Sessions Judge/F.T.C., Chitrakoot, in Sessions Trial No.33 of 2015 arising out of Case Crime No.272 of 2014 under Sections 498A, 304B, 302 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station- Rajapur, District- Chitrakoot, whereby the accused appellant Akhilesh Singh has been convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment under Section 304B I.P.C.; three years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000/- under Section 498A I.P.C. and on failure of deposit of fine to undergo additional imprisonment of one month; two years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.2,000/- under Section 4 of D.P. Act and on failure of deposit of fine to undergo additional imprisonment of one month.
All punishments are to run concurrently.

sentences.text: Basis of prosecution case in the present case is the statement of the father of the deceased as per which he had married his daughter aged 24 years with the accused as per Hindu rites and traditions after offering requisite dowry on 30.1.2013.
The husband was not satisfied with the dowry and was demanding one lakh rupees more.
The deceased was being physically and mentally tortured for the demand of dowry.
The informant was also harassed for the purpose but he showed his inability to meet the demand of dowry.
On 13.9.2014, the deceased allegedly has been done to death by her husband by pouring kerosene on her.
The brother of the informant on receiving information reached the village and found that his sister had been taken for treatment to Rajapur.
It was found that she was being treated by doctor Kanchan Singh.
The informant's daughter (deceased) allegedly informed her father of the incident.
She was later taken to Swaroop Rani Hospital, Prayagraj where she was declared brought dead.
A report has been lodged in the matter on 25.9.2014 in respect of an incident occurred on 13.9.2014.
The investigation proceeded in the matter and the inquest was conducted on 13.9.2014 at 6.30 PM.
The cause of death was the antimortem burn injuries sustained by the deceased.
The place of conduct of inquest was the mortuary at medical college, Allahabad.

Postmortem was thereafter conducted in which following cause of death has been disclosed by the autopsy surgeon:-
"Superficial to deep burn injuries present all over body except scalp, abdomen below umblicus, perineal, loin and both buttocks and feet.
Line of redness present.
Smell of kerosene present."

3. After the statement of witnesses was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. the investigating officer submitted charge-sheet against the accused on 23.11.2014 under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The case was committed to the court of Sessions where it got registered as Sessions Trial No.33 of 2015.
The accused appellant has been charged of Sections 498A, 304B IPC read with Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
Alternate charge has also been framed under Section 302 IPC.
The accused denied the charge and demanded trial.

4. During trial prosecution has produced following documentary evidence:-
"1. FIR dated 25.9.2014 as Ex.Ka.1 2. Written Report dated 25.9.2014 as Ex.Ka.1 3. P.M. Report dated 13.9.2014 as Ex.Ka.7 4.
Panchayatnama dated 13.9.2014 as Ex.Ka.4 5.

Charge-sheet dated 23.11.2014 as Ex.Ka.6"
5.
In addition to the above the prosecution has produced testimony of Head Constable Shriram Gupta as PW-1.
This witness has proved the chik FIR.
PW-2 is the informant.
PW-3 is the mother of the deceased.
PW-4 is the Investigating Officer of the case.

PW-5 is Dr. Arun Kumar Srivastava, who Akhilesh Singh vs State Of U.P. on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4323914/
2 has conducted the postmortem.

sentences.text: The aforesaid evidence has been confronted to the accused, who has denied the testimony of witnesses and has stated that he has been falsely implicated.
The accused has also stated that neither any demand of dowry was made nor has he ever tortured his wife.
He further stated that the deceased accidentally caught fire and in order to save her he also sustained firearm injuries and had to remain hospitalized for very long.
The FIR was belatedly lodged after deliberations and for such reason the uncle of the deceased has refused to depose in favour of the prosecution.
6. The defence, in addition to the above, has produced the testimony of Amar Singh, who was earlier the Pradhan and has stated that the deceased got burnt while cooking food.
Similarly DW-2 has also supported the defence case according to which the deceased got burn injuries while cooking food.
DW-3 is Dr. Kanchan Singh, who had medically examined the accused appellant and has proved the injuries on him.

7. The above evidence has been elaborately discussed by the trial court and a finding of guilt has been returned against the accused appellant under Section 304-B IPC read with Section 4 of D.P.
Act.
The appellant has been acquitted of the alternate charge under Section 302 IPC.
Life imprisonment, accordingly, has been awarded to the accused appellant.
Thus, aggrieved the appellant is before this Court.

8. Sri Jitendra Singh, learned counsel for the appellant argues that necessary ingredients to attract an offence under Section 304B and 498-A IPC are not proved and that the FIR has been lodged merely on the strength of suspicion, belatedly.
It is also submitted that the evidence on record does not justify the conviction and sentence of the accused appellant and, therefore, the appeal is liable to be allowed.

Alternatively, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the life imprisonment awarded to the accused appellant in the facts of the present case is highly excessive, particularly when the accused appellant in anxiety to save the deceased had himself sustained serious burn injuries as a result of which the accused appellant remained hospitalized for nearly four months.

9. Learned counsel submits that the accused appellant has already undergone incarceration of more than 7 years and since he has no criminal history, as such the accused appellant be let off on the sentence already undergone by him.
10. Learned AGA, on the other hand, supports the conclusions and findings of the trial court on the strength of evidence placed during trial in support of the guilt of the accused.

11. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and have perused the material brought on record,
including the lower court records.
12. It is undisputed that the marriage of the deceased was solemnized with the accused appellant on 30.1.2013 and she died an unnatural death on 13.9.2014.
The cause of death as per the postmortem report is septicemia on account of 90% burn injuries caused to the deceased.

sentences.text: It is, therefore, apparent that the unnatural death of the deceased has occurred within 7 years of the marriage.

14. We have carefully perused the testimony of PW-2 and PW-3, who are the father and mother of the deceased both of whom have alleged that the marriage was solemnized between deceased and the accused after giving various dowry items at the time of marriage.
PW-2 has specifically alleged that there was additional demand of one lakh rupees which he could not arrange that is why the deceased has been done to death.
PW-3 is also specific in alleging that the demand of dowry by the accused appellant was persistent and continued till soon before the death of the deceased.
15. From the evidence placed on record it is, therefore, apparent that the deceased has met an unnatural death within 7 years of marriage.
Evidence in support of demand of dowry soon before the death also surfaces in the facts of the case.
The postmortem report also shows that smell of kerosene was present on the body of the deceased.
16. From the above discussions it is abundantly clear that necessary ingredients to establish an offence under Section 304-B IPC are clearly shown to exist.
The conviction of the accused appellant under Section 304-B and 498A IPC read with Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act are consequently sustained.
17. Coming to the aspect of quantum of sentence the trial court has awarded maximum sentence of life to the accused appellant.

18. On the aspect of sentence we have examined the submissions of learned counsel for the appellant, wherein he has clearly stated that the conduct of the accused appellant was absolutely above board inasmuch as he took immediate measures to protect the deceased and in his anxiety to save her, he too sustained injuries and had to be admitted in hospital for nearly four months.
The injuries on the accused appellant have been proved by doctor (DW-3).
The prosecution also does not dispute this part of the testimony of the defence witnesses.
No aggravating circumstance has otherwise been placed on record which may persuade this Court to award excessive sentence to the accused appellant.
The mitigating circumstance clearly exists on record, inasmuch as the accused appellant also sustained injuries while attempting to save the deceased from the fire.
Though learned AGA has tried to submit that this injury could have been caused if the deceased had held her husband while he tried to burn her but we do not find any evidence which may indicate so.
No presumption can be drawn that the burn injuries on the accused appellant were a result of the deceased having caught him while accused was trying to ignite her.

In the absence of any positive evidence led by the prosecution to prove that the injuries on the accused appellant were caused on account of deceased having held the accused we find that the circumstance of accused appellant sustaining burn injuries can be considered as a mitigating circumstance on his part.

It is otherwise admitted that the accused appellant has no criminal history and there is no prior complaint lodged by the family members of the deceased with regard to demand of dowry against the accused.
Taking a holistic view of the evidence on record we are of the view that the minimum sentence for the offence under Section 304 IPC would sufficiently meet the ends of justice.
The accused appellant is stated to have served incarceration of more than 7 years rigorous imprisonment.

We accordingly Akhilesh Singh vs State Of U.P. on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4323914/
4 modify the sentence awarded to the accused appellant by the trial court of life, and substitute it with the sentence already undergone by the accused appellant.

sentences.text: 19. This appeal succeeds and is partly allowed.
Since the accused appellant has already remained in jail for more than seven years, as such his sentence is modified and he is released on the sentence already undergone by him.
The appellant is set to liberty on the sentence already undergone, subject to observance of Section 437A Cr.P.C. provided he is not wanted in any other case.
